target_customer: Latin American adults and career switchers who pay for live online tech and digital skills courses
problem: Demand for tech skills in Latin America outpaces affordable, practical, instructor-led training.
business_model: Consumer-paid course fees (about 100 dollars per course in 2021 per TechCrunch) with live cohorts

founders.name: Christian Patino
founders.background_notes: YC says born in the US, raised in Venezuela, based in Argentina. Company story says he could not code and enrolled in an institute, then started the school in 2014.

investors: Founders of Nubank, Rappi and Bitso

competitors.name: Digital House
competitors.what: Latin American coding school with online and in-person programs
competitors.traction_then: 28,000 students on the platform in 2020 and over 43,000 expected in 2021
competitors.funding_then: Raised over 50M dollars in 2021-03, over 80M total since 2016

competitors.name: Henry
competitors.traction_then: Had graduated 200 students and was working with 600 across Colombia, Chile, Uruguay and Argentina in 2020-12
competitors.funding_then: 1.5M dollars seed after YC Summer 2020, led by Accion Venture Lab, Emles Venture Partners and Noveus VC

competitors.name: Platzi
competitors.what: Latin American online learning platform for tech skills

technical_complexity.rationale: Live classes, a learning platform and payments; the difficulty was operations and instructor supply, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Instructor network, alumni base and brand in Argentina, but online education has low barriers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy by incumbents found; Coderhouse raised a Series A in 2021 and expanded.

market_need_then: Rapid growth in demand: revenue grew 10x yearly since 2019 to a 12M dollar run-rate by August 2021 per TechCrunch, with about 21,000 students.

identity.visual_style: Orange main brand color #FF632B per a third-party brand asset site
identity.voice_and_tone: Community and builder language aimed at career changers

branding.brand_signature: Live online cohorts and a 500,000 alumni community
branding.community_and_virality: Company pages cite 500,000+ alumni and ratings of 4.7 on Trustpilot; Latin American business press covers its story.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong regional press and large alumni base per the company, but no independent evidence the name itself drove growth.

pivots.from: In-person coding classes in Argentina, Chile, Uruguay and Peru
pivots.why: Company story says it moved online about six months before the pandemic

outcome_analysis: Coderhouse bootstrapped from 2014 using about 5,000 dollars, moved fully online in 2019, and rode the pandemic to a 12M dollar run-rate by mid-2021. It raised a 13.5M dollar Series A led by Monashees and Reach in July 2021, and now claims 500,000+ alumni and a US expansion with AI tutors. No exit or distress was found.
notes: Series A of 13.5M dollars confirmed by TechCrunch (2021-08-05), Bloomberg Linea (2021-07-30) and Reach Capital. Seed of 500K dollars is from the CEO's statement in a search result summary and its date is unknown. Later totals conflict: CB Insights shows a Series A II and total 18.17M, the company site mentions 18M, and a 2026 iProfesional piece reports an undisclosed new round; none recorded as rounds. A law firm report mentions a 68.19M figure in an unclear context; ignored. YC lists founded 2019 but the company says 2014. Pablo Ferreiro: the company story page says Patino started the school in 2014 with Ferreiro and 5,000 dollars of savings, and a 2016 Cronista article says they started the project together and that Ferreiro was country manager in Chile; neither page uses the word co-founder, so he is not listed as one. Education not found for Patino. Digital House is now sourced to TechCrunch 2021-03-25 and Henry to TechCrunch 2020-12-03, both near the as_of. Platzi still comes from an undated comparison page on Coderhouse's own site and no dated source was found.
